notes: SIXTH GENUINELY INDEPENDENT REVIEW, same peer session as #21-#25 (token 3b64530b), reviewer_was_dispatched_by_author FALSE, read-only in its own scratch clones. It returned DISAGREE first, at e4b7c6c, and the blocker it found would have made this rule USELESS ON THE MAJORITY OF REAL BRANCHES. ROUND 1, e4b7c6c, VERDICT VERBATIM: 'DISAGREE. The one change needed before merge is small (finding 2). Everything else holds or is safe while the rule ships at warn.' FINDING 2, THE BLOCKER, verbatim: 'A branch name with a slash can never be cleared by name (CONFIRMED). directory.glob("*.json") does not look in subfolders, and ids are file stems. On branch feat/x-12 the finding says add proof/feat/x-12.json before publishing. After adding exactly that file the collector still reports RepoFacts(branch=feat/x-12, proof_ids=()), and the finding repeats. The only way out is a number in the branch name: adding proof/12.json made it silent. Most branch names contain a slash, so at warn this warns on every such branch, and at deny it blocks with no fix.' THE AUTHOR'S OWN FOREIGN-REPO TEST USED THE BRANCH ship-the-widget -- no slash -- so the test that was supposed to prove the rule worked outside this repo was built by the author of the code and passed for that reason. This is the first probe matrix in this session where author bias produced a false GREEN rather than a missed edge case, and it is recorded here because the pattern matters more than the bug. Fixed by the reviewer's own first option: walk the proof directory recursively, id = path relative to the proof dir with .json stripped, joined with FORWARD SLASHES explicitly rather than os.sep, since a Windows-native separator would reproduce the identical bug platform-specifically. Verified end to end in a genuinely foreign git repo on branch feat/x-12 through the shipped bin/lwb_hook.py: it names proof/feat/x-12.json, creating exactly that path silences it. The reviewer re-confirmed at 967b652: 'With the record: RepoFacts(branch=feat/x-12, proof_ids=(feat/x-12,)) -> None. Without it: -> publishing command with no proo...' FINDING 1, HEREDOC, HALF CONFIRMED AND HALF PUSHED BACK ON BY THE AUTHOR. Its confirmed case, verbatim: '_strip_quoted removes quoted text but not unquoted heredoc bodies, and _SEGMENT_SPLIT splits on newline, so a heredoc line is read as a new command' -- cat > x.sh <<'EOF' / git push origin main / EOF gave (True, []). That is a genuine false positive, which the PR's own stated stance calls the worse direction because it trains people to ignore the warning. Fixed. THE SECOND CASE WAS NOT A FALSE POSITIVE AND WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT FIRING: in gh pr create --body-file - <<EOF, the real command is on the introducer line and gh pr create publishes whatever the body says. The implementer flagged this rather than silently suppressing it, and the author verified it rather than relaying it -- the same command with NO publish words anywhere in the body still returns (True, []), proving it matches the introducer, not the body. THE REVIEWER ACCEPTED THE PUSH-BACK, verbatim: 'Push-back: I accept it. With a body of just hello, gh pr create --body-file - <<EOF/hello/EOF -> (True, []). The gh pr create on the first line is the publish, and the heredoc only supplies the body, so this is a correct match.' FINDING 3, DENY FAILS OPEN, CONFIRMED, verbatim: 'In deny mode each of these permitted git push: bare repo -> facts=None -> None; no .git -> None; corrupt HEAD -> branch=None -> None; detached HEAD -> None. Detaching in one call and running git push origin HEAD:x in the next gets past deny. So does git -C . push, (git push), command git push, FOO=1 git push, echo $(git push) or git.exe push.' Its prescription was split deliberately: the DOCUMENTATION half was implemented in full, and the BEHAVIOURAL half was NOT, with the reason stated rather than hidden -- making repo=None fail closed at warn would fire in every directory without a .git, which is worse than the gap it closes. docs/rules/lwb-proof-required.md now states in those words that DENY IS ADVISORY, NOT A SECURITY CONTROL, lists every bypass above verbatim, says the two-step detach-then-push defeats deny entirely, and records that deny failing CLOSED on missing facts is what it would take. FINDING 5, PURITY, CONFIRMED BY EXPERIMENT RATHER THAN BY READING, and the most valuable check in the review because it is the design property the author could least verify alone. Verbatim: 'I blocked open, the os file and process calls, subprocess, socket and the pathlib.Path reads so they raise, then ran tests/core/test_lwb_proof_required.py: 35 passed in 0.06s.' That is a proof that the pure rule does no I/O, not a grep for import statements. ROUND 2, a442523: 'AGREE. The branch-name fix (finding 2) and the heredoc fix (finding 1) both work, the author's push-back holds, and deny is now documented as advisory.' It then found THREE MORE non-blocking items, all of which were fixed rather than carried, and TWO OF THEM WERE REAL PARSER BUGS rather than documentation gaps. Verbatim: 'New under-match, not a blocker: echo "a <<EOF" && git push and cat <<<word; git push both give (False, []). The heredoc stripper runs before quotes are handled and treats <<< as a heredoc, so the rest of the command is dropped.' THE HERESTRING FIX TOOK TWO ATTEMPTS AND THE FIRST ONE FAILED SILENTLY-ADJACENT: a negative lookahead alone was not enough, because <<<word still matched starting at the SECOND character, reading <<word as an introducer. It needed a lookbehind as well, and the author found that only by re-running the case rather than assuming the fix worked. Both now return True. ITS THIRD ITEM WAS THE MOST IMPORTANT, verbatim: 'The test lock is partial. test_the_shipped_default_is_warn_not_deny checks only core/policy/default.json. The two vendored default.json files are protected only because lwb_build.py --check requires the vendor copies to match source; there is no test over every shipped policy.' The vendored copies are what reach a consuming repo, and the transitive guarantee breaks the moment anyone relaxes the drift check -- for a rule that can DENY a publish. Widened to every shipped policy and PROVED NON-VACUOUS by the reviewer itself at 967b652: 'With plugins/codex/lwb/vendor/policy/default.json set to deny: FAILED ...test_no_shipped_policy_file_arms_this_rule_to_deny, 1 failed, 43 passed. I restored the file and git status --porcelain was clean.' This is what makes the position -- no shipped policy may arm deny until deny fails closed -- a decision rather than an agreement between sessions. It actually yields RepoFacts(branch=None), while a bare repo or missing .git yields event.repo is None. Same outcome, different mechanism, and a document whose job is exactness about what is NOT checked should not be loose about why. Corrected. ROUND 3, 967b652: 'AGREE holds at 967b652.
